# Source provenance

`oorexx_crypto_v0.8.3` is a qualification/provenance continuation of sealed `oorexx_crypto_v0.8.2.zip` (SHA-256 `6d99200ca29e30854ed91488b0e204fb59c379ec6dd58222fbe363e606916e27`). The Crypto source/native implementation and tests are byte-identical to v0.8.2. v0.8.3 is qualified against the user-supplied `oorexx_foreign_runtime_v0.22.2(2).zip` (SHA-256 `b4ed0572247cb68755f259b5403b9e06ace0d8a06bde39991c24416641e9def2`) and sealed Runtime Reference v0.4 (SHA-256 `c42a0c51cc5f5e26056d22db97d53eae2633141a7cebe3304b5f19b1847f957a`). Foreign Runtime v0.22.2 supersedes v0.14.0 as the qualified substrate for this candidate; Runtime Reference is unchanged.

Foreign Runtime v0.22.2 retains the Foreign Runtime facilities Crypto actually uses: runtime-loaded libffi, metadata-defined structs, typed pointer arrays, exact-binary `bytes`, resource pinning, provider threading policy and concurrent invocation. Its v0.18-v0.22.2 Python zero-copy, DLPack/tensor descriptor, device-context, optional Vulkan, and Python proxy/indexing work is additive and does not alter Crypto's direct libcrypto ABI or five compatibility exports.

Foreign Runtime v0.14.0 retains every facility used by Crypto v0.8: dynamic runtime-loaded libffi, metadata-defined structs, typed pointer arrays, exact-binary `bytes`, resource pinning, provider threading policy, call-scoped callbacks/address-space inheritance and concurrent invocation. Its new scalar-owned `.ForeignHandle`, immediate call-local `errno`, `i16`/`u16`, `.ForeignStructArray`, and PTY/poll resource semantics are orthogonal to the Crypto execution path and require no Crypto source or semantic change.

The v0.8 architecture remains unchanged. `native/openssl_direct.bridge.json` binds standard SHA, HMAC, ChaCha20, Ed25519 and BIGNUM/RSA APIs directly to system libcrypto through Foreign Runtime metadata/libffi. Package-owned native code remains only where it carries actual semantic compatibility logic: `native/crypto_compat.c` reproduces raw Edwards25519 arithmetic, current unclamped X25519, and the experimental SHA-512/Goldilocks Ed448 keypair. `libcrypto_compat.so` exposes exactly five compatibility operations and is reproducible from `native/build_crypto_compat.sh`.

Semantic compatibility is unchanged: X25519 preserves current unclamped scalar behaviour; experimental Ed448 preserves the inherited approximation; RSA preserves phi(n)-based private-exponent and textbook/text rules; ChaCha20 preserves counter 1. All native ooRexx implementations remain final fallback, and the TCP wire remains `runtime.reference/0.1`.
